classification.difficultyReason: Choose decompositions of irregular figures, infer missing lengths from horizontal and vertical alignment, and distinguish internal dashed segments from the boundary when calculating perimeter.

content.prompt: Calculate the perimeter and area of each of these figures, assuming that the non-slanting lines are either horizontal or vertical.

spec.description: Unshaded orthogonal polygon with a downward rectangular projection. All eleven printed dimensions are retained; the right side of the downward projection remains unlabelled. Ordinary source-blue outlines are rendered black under house style.
spec.answerVisibility: Question shows only the source givens; the missing length and calculated results appear only in answers.

answer.short:
$P=42\text{ m}$; $A=68\text{ m}^2$.

Find the missing vertical side, then add the boundary lengths and split the area into rectangles.
answer.worked:
The unlabelled vertical side is $5\text{ m}$ because its endpoints are level with those of the labelled $5\text{ m}$ side.
$$\begin{align*}P&=6+1+3+3+1+4+2+5+3+5+3+6\\P&=42\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
For the area, take the upper enclosing $9\text{ m}\times7\text{ m}$ rectangle, subtract the upper-left $6\text{ m}\times1\text{ m}$ gap and lower-right $1\text{ m}\times4\text{ m}$ gap, then add the downward $3\text{ m}\times5\text{ m}$ rectangle.
$$\begin{align*}A&=9\times7-6\times1-1\times4+3\times5\\A&=63-6-4+15\\A&=68\text{ m}^2.\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Three adjoining right triangles retain the stepped outer boundary, three 10 km sloping sides, all printed dimensions and two internal red dashed 2 km segments. Ordinary source-blue edges are rendered black; construction red uses the standard palette. No shading.
spec.mathematics: Top triangle has perpendicular sides 6 and 8 km; left triangle has perpendicular sides 8 and 6 km; bottom triangle has perpendicular sides 8 and 6 km. The shared internal segments are each 2 km and are excluded from perimeter.
spec.answerVisibility: All source dimensions and construction segments are permanent givens. No calculated answers appear in the question figure.

answer.short:
$P=64\text{ km}$; $A=72\text{ km}^2$.

Exclude the dashed internal segments from the perimeter and add the areas of the three right triangles.
answer.worked:
Only the solid outer boundary contributes to the perimeter; the two dashed $2\text{ km}$ segments are internal.
$$\begin{align*}P&=6+10+6+4+6+10+6+6+10\\P&=64\text{ km}.\end{align*}$$
The top, left and bottom triangles each have perpendicular sides $6\text{ km}$ and $8\text{ km}$, since $6+2=8$ and $2+4=6$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=\frac12\times6\times8+\frac12\times8\times6+\frac12\times8\times6\\A&=24+24+24\\A&=72\text{ km}^2.\end{align*}$$
